newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. after data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. after data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Tuesday, with softer U.S. Treasuries and a weaker currency weighing on prices despite the release of tame inflation reports in both countries, analysts said.

"We started off the session after our CPI report with a weaker Canadian dollar bid. It got close to C$1.389 (US$0.7199); that produced some concerns in the bond market," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed income research with ABN AMRO Bank Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.63 to C$115.90 to yield 6.755 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.73 percent. The spread between the bonds was three basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. bond markets were weaker this morning even though consumer price index reports for May showed inflation is subdued in both countries.

Statistics Canada this morning reported core CPI in Canada in May rose 1.7 percent year-over-year, below expectations of a 1.8 percent rise. U.S. core CPI rose 0.2 percent in May from April, in line with expectations.

"The bottom line here is that the data so far still suggests the U.S. Federal Reserve will not tighten rates in July, so it (the bond weakness) is a bit of a surprise. I think we'll see U.S. bonds probably bounce back at some point today," said Pyle.

The Canadian dollar opened weaker at C$1.3870 (US$0.7209) after the Canadian CPI report, released 90 minutes before the U.S. report. Traders said the absence of visible inflationary pressures in the Canadian economy would ease pressure on the Bank of Canada to tighten monetary policy in the upcoming months.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.38 to C$107.84 to yield 6.182 percent while the U.S. 10-year fell 12/32 to 6.45 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 27 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.85 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.07 percent.
